learning_outcomes.text: Combine theoretical knowledge regarding thermodynamics, machines, acoustics, and lighting technology with practical skills to evaluate the main environmental phenomena of heat transmission, acoustic waves, and light waves in living environments.
Analyze such phenomena and recognize the effects they cause on human health.
Theory of thermodynamics and heat transmission.
Theory of thermal machines and thermodynamic cycles.
Theory and technique of air conditioning.
Theory and phenomenology of indoor and outdoor microclimate of buildings.
Techniques of acoustic and lighting analysis in indoor and outdoor environments of buildings.
Evaluate the principles of thermodynamics and their application consequences.
Analyze thermal machines and their thermodynamic cycles.
Analyze the main heat exchange mechanisms.
Evaluate the quality of indoor environments and their microclimatic characteristics.
Evaluate the characteristics and main acoustic and lighting parameters and their effect on human health.

syllabus_topics: Zero principle and concept of temperature (thermal equilibrium)
Thermal machines and their energy and exergy efficiency
Construction of thermodynamic transformations on T-S and P-v graphs
Psychrometric quantities: specific humidity, relative humidity, dew point temperature, and wet-bulb temperature
Air treatments: summer treatment and winter treatment of humid air in an all-air system
Description of an air conditioning system
Application examples in civil engineering (single-layer wall, multi-layer, with and without internal heat generation, glazed walls)
Application examples in industrial field (pipe insulation, heat exchangers, cooling fin)
Lighting design for enclosed spaces: total flux method
Measurement instrumentation: luxmeter and luminance meter
Frequency bands: octaves and one-third octaves
Absorption, reflection, and transmission of acoustic energy
Sound absorption: porous sound-absorbing panels, perforated resonant absorbing panels, and vibrating panels
Sound insulation: sound insulation power and mass law
A-weighted equivalent continuous sound level LAeq,T
Elements of psychoacoustics: effects of noise on humans, shift in hearing threshold
assessment_rules: The exam will consist of 4 written questions, of which 2 will be general and 2 specific. This will be followed by a final oral exam.
